long_biography.plain_text:
Bezikian is a global luxury investor based in Switzerland. His clearest disclosed transaction came in 2023, when he invested alongside Hilco Global in a $15 million Series A round for Zelig. The company applies artificial intelligence to personalised online fashion shopping, placing his documented business activity at the intersection of investment, luxury retail and fashion technology.

His public profile also reflects sustained philanthropy. At TASIS in Switzerland, Bezikian funded an elementary-school centre named for his mother and daughter. In Lebanon, he and his daughter Ani agreed to sponsor a five-storey convention centre for the Armenian Catholicosate of Cilicia. These gifts continue a family tradition of supporting Armenian cultural, educational and religious institutions. The projects belong to the institutions they support, not to Bezikian personally.

uncertainties: No dedicated Forbes.com profile or credible Forbes identity match was found after exact-name, reversed-name, luxury, investor, Switzerland, Lebanon, billionaire and profile searches.

The exact spelling Zareh Bezikian is stable across school, church and registry sources. TechCrunch and CB Insights use Bezikian Zareh, which is treated as surname-first ordering rather than a distinct transliteration or namesake because the Swiss base, luxury-investor role and Zelig transaction agree.

No credible same-name business namesake was identified. A 2016 report about a possible Calcio Lecco acquisition also attached Bergamo residence, marriage, hockey-donation and business-associate claims to Bezikian; a subsequent published statement rejects every one of those assertions. Those facts are excluded rather than used as biography or identity anchors.

Public sources establish one disclosed Zelig transaction and describe Bezikian as a global luxury investor, but they do not expose a complete portfolio, employer, firm, office or operating role. Finance & Investments and Investor describe the best-supported current activity, not a claim that Zelig is his largest holding.

The $15 million figure is the total Zelig Series A round, not Bezikian's individual contribution. Neither that amount nor the reported company valuation is attributed to his personal stake or net worth.

The source of Bezikian's original fortune is not public. His parents' prominence, the family's philanthropic history and his capacity for large gifts do not establish inheritance, family transfer, a founder-built company or the industry that created the wealth; both wealth creation and origin therefore remain Unknown.

TASIS, its campus and the elementary-school centre are institutional assets. The Armenian Catholicosate, its convention centre and the historical Swiss foundation are likewise institutional or foundation assets. Sponsorship, donations and former board service are not treated as personal ownership.

The historical Swiss foundation record places Zareh Bezikian in Antelias and records Lebanese nationality, but the foundation became inactive in 2011. It supports identity and nationality context only, not a current residence, role, asset or business interest.

A Swiss registry aggregator describes a Zareh Bezikian in Paradiso as Italian, but it does not provide enough independent detail to establish a second nationality for the resolved individual. No secondary-nationality proposal is made.

The immutable Lebanon birth-country field was not independently confirmed by a sufficiently authoritative biographical source. Lebanese nationality, Armenian heritage and family connections to Lebanon do not prove place or country of birth, so no birth proposal is made.

No verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram or standalone personal website was found. A company website is not proposed for Zelig because public evidence establishes only an investment, not ownership or executive control of the company.
